recentItems.title: Ethnic violence in India’s Manipur through an artist’s eyes
recentItems.description:
For more than three years, India’s northeastern state of Manipur has been trapped in a cycle of ethnic violence. 
What started as a dispute between two communities about land rights, identity and tribal status, has expanded into a wider conflict.
More than 300 people have been killed and tens of thousands are living in temporary shelters.
In the capital New Delhi, the violence has found two distinct expressions -- with an art exhibition and a public protest.

Al Jazeera’s Um-e-Kulsoom Shariff reports from New Delhi, India.

recentItems.title: The business of broadcasting childhood | The Listening Post
recentItems.description:
One of the most popular genres of online content these days is made by children – or rather, made of them.

Family vlogging has become one of the internet’s most profitable genres. But questions remain over its stars’ labour protections and ability to consent to what is published about them. The Listening Post’s Tariq Nafi looks at the business of broadcasting childhood.

Featuring: 
Caymi Barrett – Former child influencer
Fortesa Latifi – Author, Like, Follow, Subscribe

recentItems.title: Yemeni forces 'reclaim' control of Bab al-Mandeb strait from Houthis
recentItems.description:
Yemeni government forces say they have taken control of Bab al-Mandeb. It's a major trade route between Asia and Europe - linking the Indian Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea – by way of the Gulf of Aden, Red Sea and Suez Canal. 
Ansar Allah Houthis are denying it.

Al Jazeera’s Osama Bin Javaid is in the studio to talk more about this and Yousef Mawry is monitoring developments from Sanaa, Yemen.

recentItems.title: Mecca defence pact faces 'first real test' as Houthis advance in Yemen, analyst says
recentItems.description:
A meeting is being held in Riyadh between government officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye to discuss regional tension and the conflict in Yemen. 
It comes as Yemeni government forces backed by Saudi Arabia, continue a counteroffensive. 

Mohamad Elmasry, a media studies professor at the Doha Institute for Graduate Studies, says the Riyadh meeting is the first real test for the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement as Yemen’s conflict escalates.

recentItems.title: Author Arundhati Roy’s fight against injustice | Talk to Al Jazeera
recentItems.description:
Since winning the Booker Prize in 1997 for her debut novel, author Arundhati Roy has not shied away from political issues. Whether she is writing fiction, nonfiction, or political essays, she focuses on social injustice.

The internationally acclaimed writer is an outspoken critic of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration. She describes India as a super poor nation, with a government that disempowers its citizens and silences dissent. Her activism goes beyond the pages of her books – she has also taken part in demonstrations against Modi’s policies. Supporters describe her as unrelenting in holding the political establishment to account. But critics accuse her of being divisive and anti-India. Despite what she calls scandal after scandal in the country, she is optimistic that political change is on the way.
